Day 1

From Hotel: 20 min → Marae Fare Opu

1. Marae Fare Opu
An ancient Polynesian ceremonial platform in Anau village, built from coral and basalt stones by early Tahitian settlers. Marae served as sites for religious ceremonies, social gatherings, and community decisions across the Society Islands.

3. Matira Point
The southernmost tip of Bora Bora's main island, where a narrow sandbar extends into the lagoon with calm, waist-deep water on both sides. Consistently ranked among the most beautiful beaches in the world, Matira is free and open to the public.

Day 2

From Hotel: 25 min → Mount Otemanu Viewpoint

1. Mount Otemanu Viewpoint
The Fitiiu Point lookout frames Mount Otemanu, the extinct basalt plug rising 727 meters at the center of Bora Bora. The summit requires technical gear, but this accessible viewpoint captures the full volcanic silhouette against the encircling reef and open Pacific.
Read more
Open 24/7
~1 hr
Fitiiu Point · northwest coast

15 min · 5 min → Vaitape Village
3. Vaitape Village
The main settlement on Bora Bora's main island, Vaitape lines the western waterfront with small boutiques, a central market, and pearl shops facing the lagoon. Farepiti Wharf, the arrival point for inter-island ferries and hotel boat transfers, sits at the center of the village.

3. Coral Garden
A shallow section of the lagoon on the western side of Motu To'opua, where dense coral formations host parrotfish, surgeonfish, and stingrays in water clear enough to see the bottom from the surface. Accessible by hotel boat from the Conrad jetty.

Local Tastes
Poisson cru
French Polynesia's national dish: raw tuna cubed and marinated in fresh lime juice, then finished in coconut milk with cucumber, tomato, and spring onion. Found at every restaurant on the island.
Local restaurants · Vaitape
Poê
A baked pudding made from ripe banana or papaya mixed with arrowroot starch, sweetened and cooked until firm. A traditional Polynesian dessert served warm or at room temperature.
Local restaurants · Vaitape
Ma'a Tinito
A slow-cooked one-pot stew of pork, kidney beans, and vegetables influenced by the Chinese immigrant community in the Society Islands. A staple at local family gatherings and casual restaurants.
Local restaurants · Vaitape
Fafaru
Raw fish soaked in seawater with fermented sea urchin and left to cure for several days. A deeply traditional delicacy with a strong fermented flavor, found at local gatherings.
Local gatherings · Vaitape area
Food Delivery
No delivery platforms serve the island. All dining is at the resort, on-property restaurants, or at restaurants in Vaitape village, reached by boat or a short bicycle ride from most properties.
Getting Around
No ride-hailing apps operate on the island. Transfers between the main motu and Vaitape use resort boats and hotel shuttles; bicycles and scooters are rentable from local operators in Vaitape for exploring the main island road.
Worth Knowing

Bora Bora's reputation as the world's most beautiful island rests on a specific geography: an extinct basalt volcano ringed by a shallow lagoon of extraordinary clarity, enclosed within a coral reef. That geometry — mountain, lagoon, reef, open Pacific — is visible from every point on the island and from the air above it. The Conrad on Motu To'opua sits inside the lagoon itself, making the reef and the mountain the view from every direction. Three days is enough to see the lagoon from its surface, from a 4×4 on the ridgeline above it, and from the air above it.
